input.prompt: First-person view of a plague doctor standing in the low cellar under a poor house in a remote mountain village, present day: rough stone walls, a low ceiling of old dark wooden beams with a thick beam across the middle, a beaten earth floor; on the left steep wooden steps come down from an open trapdoor in the ceiling; along the right wall wooden shelves with dusty glass jars; a few empty jute potato sacks and a plastic bucket on the floor; an old thin mattress on the floor with a stained grey blanket. A single bare bulb hangs from a beam. One figure, close to the viewer: from the thick beam just in front of the viewer, in the middle of the frame, hangs a young man of about twenty who has become a cocoon, as big as a man and filling half the height of the picture. His whole body, curled up with the knees pulled to the chest, is wrapped in a thick tangle of grey and black threads, like mould or old cobwebs, that grow out of his own skin and fasten him to the beam; only his face is free, at the viewer's eye level and turned towards the viewer: very pale, smooth and moist, the eyes open, dark and wet, the lips grey. Long threads hang down from the cocoon to the earth floor. He hangs perfectly still, as if asleep with his eyes open. Behind him the rest of the cellar is visible. No hands, arms or objects belonging to the viewer are visible in the frame. Realistic photograph, evenly exposed, everything clearly readable, no dramatic shadows. 16:9, no text, no border.
